findings.claim: Removing the `bodyCache.formData` fast path makes `parseFormData` unconditionally call `arrayBuffer()`, which will throw when the request body has already been consumed (e.g. a prior `c.req.formData()` / `c.req.parseBody()` call).
findings.rationale: This guard existed precisely to serve a request whose body was already read and cached as FormData. Without it, the very next line (`await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()`) runs on a disturbed/locked stream and rejects with a TypeError ("Body is unusable" / "Body has already been read"), so any handler that calls `c.req.formData()` before `c.req.parseBody()` (or calls `parseBody` twice, since the code below caches into `bodyCache.formData`) now fails at runtime instead of returning the cached data. It also silently discards a cached FormData that callers may have populated/modified. I'm fairly confident this is a behavior-breaking regression unless the caller was changed to guarantee an unread body.

findings.claim: `arrayBuffer()` is called without consulting `request.bodyCache.arrayBuffer`, so an already-buffered body is not reused.
findings.rationale: Hono's `HonoRequest.bodyCache` also caches `arrayBuffer`; with the FormData short-circuit gone, this path is now the only route and still ignores every cache entry. If `c.req.arrayBuffer()` was called earlier, this throws instead of reusing the cached buffer. Lower confidence (depends on how callers of `parseFormData` are guarded elsewhere), but worth a second look given the guard above was removed.
